title.value: ComplexDataLab at WNUT-2020 Task 2: Detecting Informative COVID-19 Tweets by Attending over Linked Documents
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the very beginning of the paper.
title.quote: ComplexDataLab at WNUT-2020 Task 2: Detecting Informative COVID-19 Tweets by Attending over Linked Documents

analysis.description: The paper presents G APFORMER, a model that classifies tweets as informative or not by reformulating the problem as a graph classification task, utilizing not only the tweet but also connected web pages and entities. It leverages a pre-trained language model and connections between nodes to learn a pooled representation, outperforming several baselines in the identification of informative COVID-19 related tweets.

type.justification: The paper involves experiments and comparisons of the proposed model against several baselines, indicating that it is empirical research.
type.quote: We show it outperforms several competitive baselines and present ablation studies supporting the benefit of the linked information.

name.justification: The paper deals with processing tweets and other related text data to classify them based on their informativeness, which falls under Natural Language Processing.
name.quote: Given the global scale of COVID-19 and the flood of social media content related to it, how can we find informative discussions?

name.justification: The paper discusses the use of graph structures and GraphSAGE convolutions in its methodology, which is a key component of Graph Neural Networks.
name.quote: We reformulate the task as graph classification, where each instance is a single graph comprised of one tweet as well as the extracted entities and documents.

name.justification: G APFORMER is the main model being proposed and discussed in the paper.
name.quote: We present here G APFORMER, which combines multiple sources of information - the tweet, content of linked web pages, and information about named entities related to the tweet - to improve detection of informative content.

is_contributed.justification: G APFORMER is introduced in this paper as a new model for the specific task.
is_contributed.quote: We present G APFORMER, which detects informative Covid-19 tweets, using a graph classification system that leverages articles and entities.

is_executed.justification: The paper discusses experiments conducted using G APFORMER, which implies execution.
is_executed.quote: Our experiments show G APFORMER outperforms 7 baselines.

is_compared.justification: The model is compared against several baselines as part of the empirical study.
is_compared.quote: We show it outperforms several competitive baselines and present ablation studies supporting the benefit of the linked information.
